brief: Macro backdrop (a global bond selloff, yields near multi-decade highs, rising energy prices) weighs on crypto and risk assets. Friday's August core CPI beat expectations, pushing market-implied September rate-hike odds to around 85%; GIR now expects a 25bp September FOMC hike, driven less by a change in its inflation view than by the Committee's reluctance to surprise markets. From Friday's close to Monday Asia trading, BTC fell 2.72%, ETH rose 2.56%, gold fell 2.34%, and the S&P 500 and Nasdaq closed lower. ETH's relative outperformance was notable: intraday CPI-day gains in equities, BTC and gold faded, but ETH held near its rally high of $2.6k, its best level since January, and spot ETH ETFs took in net inflows (+$197m for the week) while spot BTC ETFs saw outflows every session (-$463m total). This week brings the CLARITY Act's procedural vote (15 September) and the FOMC meeting (15-16 September); a new Senate Republican draft addressing stablecoin-reward and ethics-restriction sticking points lifted Polymarket's odds of the bill passing this year from 22% to 32%. BTC perp funding rose despite spot's pullback even as CME's front-month BTC basis compressed to 4.20% from 5.81%, and both BTC and ETH 25-delta risk reversals stayed positive.
